standards.standard_name: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: The assessment includes the individual's history of addictive behaviors.

findings.description: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: The organization obtains the individual's history of alcohol use, drug use, nicotine use, and other addictive behaviors. The history includes the following information: Age of onset; Method of acquiring substance; Duration; Patterns of use (for example, continuous, episodic, binge); Frequency, amounts, and route of the substance that is taken.
findings.finding: Assessment documents age of onset (17), duration (since age 33 for problematic use), patterns (daily), frequency and amounts (5-7 drinks per day), but lacks documentation of method of acquiring substances and route of administration, and does not address nicotine use history.

citations.text: Patient began social drinking at age 17. Consumption remained at recreational levels until age 33 when his long-term relationship of 4 years ended. Following the separation, drinking escalated from 2-3 drinks on weekends to daily consumption of 5-7 drinks.
citations.relevance: Documents onset, duration, patterns, frequency and amounts but missing method of acquisition and route

citations.text: Cannabis: occasional use, 1-2 times per month, recreational. Denies use of opioids, stimulants, benzodiazepines, or other substances.
citations.relevance: Documents other substance use but lacks comprehensive nicotine history

findings.remediation: Complete substance use history by documenting method of acquiring alcohol, route of administration, and comprehensive nicotine use history.

findings.description: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: The assessment includes the following: Consequences of substance use; Physical problems related to use; Family substance use history; Spirituality and cultural factors; Readiness to change; Current living arrangements.
findings.finding: Assessment documents consequences of substance use, physical problems, family substance use history, spirituality, and readiness to change, but current living arrangements are not specifically documented.

citations.text: Occupational: tardiness to work approximately twice per week due to hangovers, difficulty concentrating on tasks.

citations.text: Father had problematic alcohol use throughout patient's childhood and never sought treatment.

citations.text: Patient acknowledges drinking is 'probably a problem' but expresses ambivalence about full abstinence. Contemplation stage of change.
citations.relevance: Documents readiness to change

findings.remediation: Document patient's current living arrangements as part of comprehensive addiction assessment.

findings.description: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: Assessments of the individual served contain information about the following: Previous care, treatment, or services; Response to previous care, treatment, or services; Current risks and history of risks related to substance use (likelihood of engaging in substance use or substance use-related behaviors that carry significant risk for serious medical, psychological, social, or financial/legal consequences); Acute intoxication and/or withdrawal potential; Needs related to medications for substance use disorders.
findings.finding: Assessment comprehensively documents all required elements: no previous treatment, current risks (occupational impairment, health consequences), withdrawal potential assessment through CIWA-Ar monitoring, and medication needs with naltrexone consideration.

findings.description: For organizations providing care, treatment, or services to individuals with addictions: The organization uses an evidence-based, multidimensional admission assessment that includes, at a minimum, mental health, medical, and substance-use history for placement of the individual at the appropriate level of care.
findings.finding: Assessment includes comprehensive mental health history (anxiety, depression, no prior treatment), medical history (hypertension, elevated liver enzymes), and detailed substance use history, with appropriate placement in IOP level of care based on assessment findings.
